title: Showtime at the O’Dome: McMiller’s Career-High 42 Powers Florida Past UCF, 95-65
excerpt: Kiyomi McMiller scored a career-high 42 points and Vivian Iwuchukwu added 20 as Florida rolled past UCF 95-65 in Gainesville.

cover.alt: Florida guard Kiyomi McMiller poses with students after scoring a career-high 42 points against UCF on Nov. 5, 2026. UAA Communications photo.
cover.filename: Kiyomi McMiller after career-high 42 vs UCF - UAA Communications.jpg

blocks.text: By Loren Meadows, GatorBaitMedia.com and host of The Gator Lowdown with Loren Meadows

runs.t: By Loren Meadows, GatorBaitMedia.com and host of The Gator Lowdown with Loren Meadows

blocks.text: This evening, Florida’s basketball teams took part in a rare doubleheader that saw the Florida women take on UCF, followed by the top-ranked men’s basketball team facing Jacksonville and former Florida assistant Jordan Mincey. While fans, including the Rowdy Reptiles, showed up to get a good seat for the men’s home opener, what they got was an Allen Iverson-, Dawn Staley- and Caitlin Clark-like show from junior point guard Kiyomi McMiller. The second-team preseason All-SEC pick from Silver Springs, Maryland, was all in her bag tonight with a quick first step, elite ball handling and efficient scoring on her way to a career-high 42-point explosion that led Florida to a 95-65 win over UCF. McMiller’s 42 points were the fourth-highest output in Gators history. Following a 31-point effort Monday against Bucknell, she became just the fifth player in school history to score 30 or more points in back-to-back games.

Iwuchukwu averaged just 2.9 points per game last season in a more workmanlike role at USC. blocks.text: “It all started from the summertime. Obviously, this is a new role for me, but the coaches really prepared me to excel in the role. All summer, I really worked on that. blocks.text: Regardless of the performances, what coach Tammi Reiss was most pleased with was the energy of both her team and the O’Dome crowd:

runs.t: Regardless of the performances, what coach Tammi Reiss was most pleased with was the energy of both her team and the O’Dome crowd:

blocks.text: “You know I love being a part of Gator Nation, the Gator family. It’s one of the greatest sports environments in college athletics. The brand is unbelievable, so I want them coming out and supporting us. They come out to every sport here — you see them at softball, volleyball, baseball. So I love the fact that they knew it was a doubleheader and they came to get their seats for the men’s game, but I am hoping, like Vivian said, you build it brick by brick and then by the time you’re competing for championships, this O’Dome is sold out. That is our goal, seat by seat, fan by fan, but there is nothing like having students. It is a different atmosphere. I love the ruckus and I hope they keep coming out and supporting us.”
